market_question: Fed rate cut by September 2026 meeting?
reasoning: The market's 14% probability of a rate cut between Dec 2025 and Sep 2026 is far below the consensus expectation that the Fed will continue easing in 2026. The Fed's dot plot and market-implied rates suggest cuts are likely to bring the federal funds rate down to around 3.0% by end-2026 from a projected 3.5% at the start of the window. Barring a severe inflation resurgence, at least one cut in the Jan-Sep 2026 period is probable.
evidence_points: Federal Reserve dot plot (Dec 2024) shows median year-end 2026 fed funds rate at 2.9% (midpoint) vs. 3.4% for 2025, implying ~50bps of cuts in 2026.
CME FedWatch indicates futures pricing in multiple cuts by mid-2026, with the rate approaching 3.0% by September 2026.
Economist surveys (Bloomberg, Reuters) broadly expect the Fed to ease in 2026 as inflation continues to moderate toward 2%.
The window covers six FOMC meetings (Jan, Mar, May, Jun, Jul, Sep) and potential emergency cuts, providing ample opportunities for a single cut.
